argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than clean certification. The admissible record supports certification only if it is expressly caveated by disclosing the unresolved fraud-dispute-review limitation for the named launch use case. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports launch readiness in the aggregate, while public risk-management and model-card guidance supports deployment with documented limitations and active monitoring. The same record does not support treating the draft runbook as complete governance cover, because the fraud dispute review slice remains below target and the draft mitigation still has TBD owner and threshold fields.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the compliance question, and no urgency rationale is relied on here.
claims_about_policy: The policy record cuts against an unqualified compliance finding, not against all certification. The admissible policy text says certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The separate release-policy note says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On that record, the compliant reading is caveated certification with explicit disclosure of the unresolved limitation, not clean certification based on aggregate metrics alone.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation under the stated policy because key fields remain TBD.
Public guidance about monitoring and model cards does not by itself satisfy the internal approval predicate.
No admissible evidence here shows approved risk acceptance, approved mitigation, or a finalized disclosure package already issued.
